segments.title: 第154章 神奇的蝴蝶效應
segments.content:
Rejuvenation: The Verdant Years Chapter 154: A Miraculous Butterfly Effect

Throughout December, Qian Zhou was in a very good mood.

At first, it was because, in addition to "I'm Really Not a Star" and "The Literary Era," several more of his books had surpassed one thousand average subscriptions.

Among them, two even showed signs of becoming boutique works.

Then there was Zao Shui Hui Zhang Gao's "The Literary Era," whose average subscriptions had slowly risen to around 2500. With another recommendation spot at the end of the year, it would likely have a chance to touch the threshold of a boutique work.

He would then have another great general under his command.

For a new editor, this was incredibly exciting.

Not only was it an affirmation of his personal judgment and ability, but it also meant tangible salary commissions and bonuses.

But what Qian Zhou hadn't expected was that, starting from the beginning of December, the stats for Chong Ran's "I'm Really Not a Star" had begun to soar at an unbelievable speed.

Especially since he hadn't even had time to arrange a recommendation spot for "I'm Really Not a Star" this month. It was purely natural growth, yet it still managed to maintain at least 1,000 new subscriptions every day.

And it showed no signs of slowing down.

For the first week, Qian Zhou hadn't even noticed.

After all, he had to personally click into the backend page to view the stats.

And editors usually focused more of their energy on new books.

For older books that were already on sale, checking them once a week was considered frequent.

Especially for an author like Chong Ran, who had already broken the boutique line but whose results were far from reaching ten thousand subscriptions, his book could only be left to simmer for the time being.

It wasn't until the middle of the month, when Qian Zhou routinely glanced at the stats for Chong Ran's book, that he realized something was amiss.

How had the average subscriptions risen to six or seven thousand?

Weren't they just a little over four thousand at the beginning of the month?

Pulling up the data for the month, Qian Zhou's face went blank, a little confused.

Without the boost of a recommendation, it had gained twenty to thirty thousand subscriptions in half a month.

Was this even human?

Could it be that word of mouth had exploded, so readers were spontaneously recommending it, attracting a lot of new readers?

But this rate of increase had been going on for too long, hadn't it?

It was only then that Qian Zhou went to check Chong Ran's review section and slowly figured out the situation.

It turned out that Chong Ran had written an original song in the book, and he had actually found someone to sing it and released it online.

In the end, the song was picked up by a certain TV drama, bought to be its theme song, and was even sung to fame.

Qian Zhou shared this in the editors' group chat. Whether it was the editors in his team or the editor-in-chief Hongdou, everyone was dumbfounded. They had truly never encountered a situation like this before.

And so, this matter began to circulate through the various offices of Wen Yue Group like a piece of fresh gossip.

If the matter had ended there, it would have been nothing much.

It would just be a case of a certain author who was truly talented and also lucky, who managed to catch this heaven-sent fortune from off-site traffic and had a hearty meal.

Judging by the current trend, "I'm Really Not a Star" would break eight thousand average subscriptions by the end of the month.

It would probably reach ten thousand subscriptions next month.

One had to know, this was ten thousand subscriptions in the year 2014. In the entire ten-plus years of the website, only two or three hundred books had accumulated this achievement.

And this was the cumulative total.

If you looked at ongoing books with ten thousand subscriptions, the entire Qidian website probably couldn't even count 50.

One only had to look at the rankings for "I'm Really Not a Star" these past few days to know.

On the overall chart, "I'm Really Not a Star" was already ranked 28th.

On the bestseller chart, which was ranked based on sales data, it had even reached 19th place on the entire website, thanks to the continuous support of readers drawn in during this period.

For a new author, this was, without a doubt, a miracle.

And under such circumstances, a new employee in the operations department was assigned an internship task.

The supervisor required each of them to find a web novel they were interested in, analyze and plan for it, and propose a suitable promotion plan.

One employee quite liked reading "I'm Really Not a Star" and used it as a case study.

And so...

Chong Ran: I do know her, actually. What's up?

Qian Zhou: You really know her... You're too awesome.

Chong Ran: If my editor wants an autograph, I can help you get one.

Qian Zhou: No, no, no, that's not what I mean. I'm here to tell you some good news.

Chong Ran: Hmm?

Qian Zhou: It's like this, the operations department came up with a plan. Didn't they hear that you gave that song of yours, "Annual Rings," to Yuan Wanqing to sing?

Qian Zhou: And that she even made the song a hit.

Qian Zhou: So, operations was thinking, they sent an invitation to Yuan Wanqing's work email, asking if she would be willing to accept an interview and collaboration event with us.

Qian Zhou: To be honest, it was just a long shot. After all, although our Wen Yue Group is a subsidiary of Penguin, the Qidian side of things basically has the status of a stepson, we don't usually get much support.

Qian Zhou: Yuan Wanqing's popularity is sky-high right now, she might not have paid us any mind.

Qian Zhou: Who knew, the operations team sent the email in the afternoon and got a reply in the evening, saying it was no problem. Then she gave us a few open time slots and told us to pick one.

Qian Zhou: Holy crap! As soon as I got this news, I came looking for you right away. This is a massive opportunity, Brother, you have to seize it!

My goodness... he's gotten so excited he's calling me Brother.

The corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched. He felt a persistent sense of unease in his heart.

Chong Ran: So... is there anything I need to do for this event?

Qian Zhou: That's what I'm here to ask you. Are you free this weekend?

Chong Ran: Um... I should be.

The unease in Li Luo's heart grew more pronounced.

Qian Zhou: Then can you come to the city? Yuan Wanqing's company is right here in Yuhang City. We'll send people over to conduct an exclusive interview with her there.

Qian Zhou: You'll be invited to have a simple dialogue and exchange with Yuan Wanqing, talk about your respective creative journeys and whatnot.

Qian Zhou: What do you think?

What do I think?

Li Luo felt goosebumps rise all over his body.

I think it's not a good idea at all!

Which heaven-defying operations staffer came up with this idea?!

He was already a little embarrassed to meet that Auntie Yuan.

And now you!

Not only are you arranging for me to meet her, but you also want me to share my own creative journey?

What do I have to share?

Share why I decided to write a harem novel?!

And...

Chong Ran: Boss, I'm still young. I don't want to show my face. If I get recognized at school, it'll be a big hassle for me.

Qian Zhou: Oh, that.

Qian Zhou: That's not a big problem. We can help you cover your face. You just don't have to appear on camera, just do the interview.

Qian Zhou: After all, Yuan Wanqing's face is the main point. You're mainly contributing the work.

Those words stung a little.

But with his editor putting it that way, Li Luo found it much more acceptable.

Chong Ran: What about after the interview? What's the overall plan?

Qian Zhou: Oh, right, I forgot to tell you.

Qian Zhou: Your book is over nine hundred thousand words now, right?

Qian Zhou: According to the rules, books with over one million words are ranked by their performance. The higher the rank, the sooner they enter channel distribution.

Qian Zhou: If you accept this interview event, we'll arrange for your book to be put on the channels the very next day.

Qian Zhou: Paired with a nationwide push of the subsequent interview content, we'll direct the audience to the main site or various channel distribution platforms to firmly catch this wave of traffic.

Qian Zhou: Chong Ran, you have to think this through. If this blows up, will your royalties still be just tens of thousands of yuan?

Qian Zhou: Earning a hundred thousand a month won't be a dream!

Qian Zhou: Other people only start looking for a job after graduating from university, but you haven't even started university yet, and you're already a winner in life!

Qian Zhou: If you can't make up your mind, you can discuss it with your parents tomorrow. I'm available to talk anytime.

It was clear that for this book with the potential to become a massive hit, Qian Zhou was pleading earnestly, pulling out all the stops.

Li Luo thought it over and understood the many benefits. He remembered that he had already promised Yan Zhusheng he would go to her house this Saturday to meet Auntie Yuan.

And so, he gritted his teeth.

Chong Ran: I understand, Editor. Just go ahead and arrange it for me. I'll be there this weekend.

Qian Zhou: Great!

Qian Zhou: If you're okay with it, I'll reply to the operations department immediately.

Qian Zhou: Wait for me this weekend. I'll come over with them then.

Qian Zhou: If your parents are worried, I can come to your house to pick you up directly. If your parents want to come along, that's no problem either, I'll arrange it.

Chong Ran: We can talk about that later.

Qian Zhou: okok, that's all for now, talk to you later.

After ending the private chat with his editor, Li Luo didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

He never would have thought that a single song, "Annual Rings," would trigger such a long chain reaction.

He had originally thought he had just sold a song and earned tens of thousands of yuan.

But thanks to "Annual Rings" and his connection with Yan Zhusheng, he got to know Yuan Wanqing and Luo Fei, established a line with Huayue Film and Television Company, and sold two more songs on the side.

And "Annual Rings," as the theme song, directly caused Yuan Wanqing to make a comeback, riding on the hype of the controversial TV drama "The Legend of Yaochi."

In the end, it even affected the promotion priority of his own book within Wen Yue Group.

He had to admit, sometimes things were truly miraculous.

When Li Luo wrote books in his past life, Qidian's channel distribution was already in decline. He had basically never enjoyed its benefits.

But he had heard about those channel big shots from back in the day, whose results on the main site might have been average, but once their one-million-word book hit the channels, they could make a fortune.

If he could seize this opportunity...

Li Luo stroked his chin thoughtfully, wondering if he would have the money to buy a subway station commercial property very soon.

(End of this chapter)
